children: Gold is steady in early Asian trade. Investors are closely watching the U.S. CPI data due later Wednesday for clues on the Federal Reserve's interest rate path. A hotter-than-expected print could drive expectations that the Fed might raise interest rates at its next meeting. Higher rates typically diminish the allure of the non-interest-bearing precious metal. Markets are also focusing their attention on Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh's speech on Friday, Critical Metals CEO Tony Sage says in a note. Spot gold is flat at $4,160.14 an ounce. (amanda.lee@wsj.com)
